title: Rochdale does it again! Littleborough takeaway crowned North West’s best as borough celebrates extraordinary run of success
excerpt: Tandoori Flames in Littleborough has won North West Takeaway of the Year at ARTA 2026 — following River Beal’s 2025 win and Wild Ginger’s restaurant title, giving Rochdale borough three regional awards in two years.
body:
Rochdale borough is celebrating another remarkable victory on the national hospitality stage after Tandoori Flames in Littleborough was crowned North West Takeaway of the Year — bringing the prestigious title home for the second consecutive year.

And there is an even bigger story behind the award. In just two years, businesses from Littleborough and Milnrow have claimed three major regional titles at the Asian Restaurant and Takeaway Awards (ARTA), competing against establishments from some of the North West’s largest towns and cities.

It is an extraordinary achievement for the borough’s independent hospitality industry and a reminder that some of the region’s most celebrated food businesses are found right here on our doorstep.

A victory for Littleborough — and the whole borough

Tandoori Flames, based on Church Street in Littleborough, received the Regional Takeaway of the Year award at a ceremony at the London Hilton on Park Lane on Monday, 12 October.

More than 1,250 businesses from across the United Kingdom were nominated for the 2026 awards, which celebrate excellence in Asian restaurants and takeaways.

The Littleborough business emerged victorious in the North West takeaway category, having been shortlisted alongside competitors from Manchester, Bolton, Wigan, Wilmslow and elsewhere in the region.

The awards take into account customer nominations, review scores, food hygiene ratings and assessments by a judging panel.

For the team behind Tandoori Flames, it is recognition that extends well beyond Littleborough, putting an independent neighbourhood takeaway firmly in the regional spotlight.

Two years, three major awards — and all from Rochdale

What makes this year’s result especially significant is that Rochdale borough has now secured the North West Takeaway of the Year title in consecutive years, through two different businesses.

In 2025, River Beal Indian Takeaway in Milnrow was crowned North West Takeaway of the Year.

That same year, Wild Ginger Restaurant in Littleborough won North West Restaurant of the Year.

Now, in 2026, Tandoori Flames has continued the borough’s winning streak by bringing the takeaway award back to Rochdale borough.

Three regional awards. Two consecutive years. Three independent businesses from the same borough.

And the success did not end with the winner.

River Beal was shortlisted again in the North West’s top ten takeaways for 2026, meaning two Rochdale borough businesses were recognised among the regional contenders this year.

It is an impressive concentration of award-winning establishments within a relatively small geographical area, demonstrating just how strongly local independent businesses can compete on a much larger stage.

A triumph for independent businesses

Behind every takeaway counter and restaurant kitchen are people working long hours, preparing food, serving customers and trying to build something that lasts.

For independent hospitality businesses, that work has become increasingly difficult.

Rising energy bills, food costs, employment expenses and other operating pressures have placed considerable strain on restaurants and takeaways across Britain.

Yet businesses such as Tandoori Flames, River Beal and Wild Ginger have continued to earn national recognition.

Their achievements are particularly encouraging because they demonstrate that smaller, community-based establishments can compete successfully for major industry honours.

These are not simply awards for food. They recognise the people, businesses and skills that contribute to the character of our towns and villages.

And they highlight the importance of customers who continue to support independent businesses rather than automatically turning to national chains.

Rochdale represented on the national stage

This year’s awards ceremony brought together leading chefs, restaurateurs and hospitality figures from across the country.

Among the guests was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, alongside actor and dancer Lauren Gottlieb and singer and former Indian parliamentarian Hans Raj Hans.

The evening was hosted by television presenter Samantha Simmonds and comedian Paul Sinha.

Mohammed Munim, founder and chief executive of ARTA, congratulated the winners and finalists, praising their dedication, creativity and commitment to maintaining high standards despite the difficulties facing the hospitality industry.

He also emphasised the wider importance of Asian restaurants and takeaways in British communities, from providing employment to contributing to the country’s culinary heritage.

For Rochdale, that contribution is visible in the independent establishments that have become familiar fixtures of local life.

Something worth celebrating

Rochdale often finds itself in the headlines for difficult reasons. Economic pressures, deprivation and the challenges facing local businesses are important stories that deserve scrutiny.

But there are other stories worth telling, too.

Stories about people succeeding, businesses growing in reputation and communities producing something that is recognised far beyond the borough’s boundaries.

The achievements of Tandoori Flames, River Beal and Wild Ginger belong firmly in that category.

To see three regional titles awarded to independent businesses in Littleborough and Milnrow over just two years is something the entire borough can take pride in.

For the staff working in those kitchens, the owners who have invested in their businesses and the customers who have supported them, these awards represent something genuinely special.

Rochdale Daily extends its warmest congratulations to Tandoori Flames on its 2026 victory, to River Beal on another outstanding year of recognition, and to Wild Ginger for helping establish this extraordinary record of local success.

At a time when independent businesses need support more than ever, there has rarely been a better reason to celebrate Rochdale’s local food industry.

Have you eaten at Tandoori Flames, River Beal or Wild Ginger? We’d love to hear your experiences. Leave a comment below and help us celebrate the independent businesses making Rochdale proud.
